headline: High-risk filesystem and shell asymmetry: AutoGPT can act on files and shell commands while dagster is readless and networkless, making prompt-injection and cascading-error pathways the main concern.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and access the filesystem, so if it ingests dagster-produced artifacts or logs as instructions, prompt injection is plausible. Dagster has no clipboard/MCP/browser channel and no direct output channel documented here, so the pathway is indirect rather than default. Uncertainty about the exact handoff keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF dagster writes attacker-controlled text into a file that AutoGPT later reads as instructions
IF an operator manually copies dagster output into AutoGPT prompts
mitigations: Restrict AutoGPT to a dedicated input directory
Prefix all dagster outputs with non-executable markers
Review any file-to-prompt bridge before use
Disable manual copy-paste of untrusted pipeline text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between dagster outputs and AutoGPT prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT can touch the filesystem and make allowlisted network egress, but the profile does not show sensitive data classes or shared workspace with dagster. Dagster is readless and networkless here, so there is no documented path for it to exfiltrate data. The pair therefore has a limited leakage surface unless an operator places sensitive files into AutoGPT's workspace.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in AutoGPT's filesystem workspace
IF AutoGPT is configured to send file contents through its allowlisted egress
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of AutoGPT's workspace
Use a separate non-sensitive staging directory
Audit allowlisted destinations before running
Rotate any secrets that may already be present in shared folders
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can write via shell and filesystem, while dagster cannot write files, modify git state, or use subprocesses in this profile. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only plausible conflict is operator-mediated sharing of mutable resources, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory through external orchestration
IF AutoGPT is given git or database credentials outside this profile
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent
Avoid shared git branches during runs
Serialize any manual handoffs
Check for stale lockfiles before execution
requires-engineering: add resource locking in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate actions from its own reasoning, and dagster is a data-orchestration tool that may consume upstream outputs in pipelines. If dagster treats AutoGPT output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream work products. The profiles do not prove a direct default handoff, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF dagster ingests AutoGPT-produced files or metadata without validation
IF AutoGPT output is used as a pipeline input or decision artifact
mitigations: Add validation before dagster consumes AutoGPT output
Require human review for generated artifacts
Use schema checks on all handoffs
Log and reject malformed outputs
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and both profiles show empty data_classes_touched and no secrets handled. With no compliance mismatch evidence, a residency or retention breach is not established. The other agent is not cited separately because the profiles lack any compliance-specific surface to compare.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data classes not shown here
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment
Review retention settings if regulated data is added
Keep PHI and PII out of both agents until controls are defined
